result.title: Rethinking Post-Training Quantization for Large Vision-Language Models
result.summary: Post-training quantization (PTQ) compresses large vision-language models (LVLMs) by calibrating quantization parameters on a small dataset without retraining. However, despite increasingly sophisticated calibration strategies, prior methods suffer substantial performance degradation under low-bit weight--activation quantization. To understand this degradation, we locate where quantization error is concentrated and examine the corresponding weight and activation distributions. We observe that a few outliers dominate the ranges shared by per-channel (PC) weights and per-token (PT) activations, leaving insufficient resolution for most values and mapping many of them to zero. These findings motivate a shift in focus from calibration refinement to the underlying quantization representation. We therefore present Rotate-and-Refine Quantization (RRQ) as a simple, effective baseline for LVLM PTQ, combining local Hadamard transforms with group quantization and efficient group-aware execution. Across 8 multimodal tasks and diverse quantization settings, RRQ substantially outperforms baselines while reducing inference time and memory usage. At W4A4, it retains over 96\% of full-precision performance on 8B models and over 99\% on a 32B model, compared with less than 8\% for these baselines. The source code is publicly available at https://github.com/kmc3661/RRQ

AI.brief_summary: 论文诊断 LVLM 低比特后训练量化的性能退化来源，发现 per-channel 权重与 per-token 激活共享的量化范围被少数离群值主导，使多数数值分辨率不足甚至被映射为零；据此提出 Rotate-and-Refine Quantization，用局部 Hadamard 变换结合分组量化与分组感知执行，在 8 项多模态任务上优于基线。
AI.relevance_reason: 「多数数值被压到零、分辨率不足」可视为内部状态信息坍缩的一种外显形式，或可作为扰动手段检验视觉细节在 VLM 内部表示中的保留与因果贡献，但与 latent 推理过程的联系尚待核查。
